stages.title: WHAT AGRICULTURAL GEOGRAPHY STUDIES
stages.terms: Agriculture is a leading primary activity because it draws directly on land, water, climate, soil and labour.
stages.mechanism: Agriculture is a leading primary activity because it draws directly on land, water, climate, soil and labour.
stages.consequence: Rice appears in humid eastern and deltaic belts because water and level alluvial land favour it, but irrigated rice can also appear in drier north-western districts.
stages.trap: Primary activity does not mean technologically primitive.
stages.answer: A good GS-I opening line is: Agricultural geography explains the spatial organisation of production through the interaction of ecological suitability and human choice.

stages.title: THE SIX CONTROLS OF AGRICULTURE
stages.terms: Black soil supports cotton in parts of the Deccan because it retains moisture, but cotton also grows on alluvial soils where climate, irrigation and markets are favourable.
stages.mechanism: Black soil supports cotton in parts of the Deccan because it retains moisture, but cotton also grows on alluvial soils where climate, irrigation and markets are favourable.
stages.consequence: A fertile soil without suitable temperature, water, labour or access does not automatically become a productive farming belt.
stages.trap: Irrigation reduces rainfall uncertainty; it does not remove heat, drainage or market limits.
stages.answer: For a location question, organise the answer under physical controls and human controls, then show their interaction.

stages.title: MAJOR AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS
stages.terms: A farming system tells us how land, labour, animals, capital and markets are combined.
stages.mechanism: Wet-rice cultivation may be highly intensive because much labour is applied to a small field, even when mechanisation is limited.
stages.consequence: A tea plantation is commercial and export-oriented, but it is a different system from a commercial grain farm.
stages.trap: Shifting cultivation and plantation agriculture are not synonyms.
stages.answer: Commercial orientation asks how strongly production is aimed at the market.

stages.title: VON THUNEN — WHY DISTANCE STILL MATTERS
stages.terms: Do not call the model obsolete merely because technology changes distance penalties.
stages.mechanism: Do not call the model obsolete merely because technology changes distance penalties.
stages.consequence: They do not make freight, freshness, delivery frequency or access disappear.
stages.trap: A cold chain can move the belt outward, but it adds cost and requires reliable logistics.
stages.answer: Von Thunen is a location model, not a climate classification.

stages.title: WORLD AGRICULTURAL REGIONS AND CROP REQUIREMENTS
stages.terms: A crop region is a bundle of suitability, not a single climatic number.
stages.mechanism: A crop region is a bundle of suitability, not a single climatic number.
stages.consequence: Crop requirements are broad guides, not rigid thresholds.
stages.trap: A historical production belt is not automatically the current top-ranking belt.
stages.answer: World regions become memorable when each is tied to one climate pattern, one production system and one market or labour feature.

stages.title: FROM SUBSISTENCE TO COMMERCIALISATION
stages.terms: A vegetable-growing district can commercialise only when production is matched by roads, grading, aggregation, storage and buyers.
stages.mechanism: Commercialisation is produced by water + technology + connectivity + institutions + demand.
stages.consequence: Cold chain changes distance costs but can add capital, energy and bargaining risks.
stages.trap: More inputs do not automatically mean more net income.
stages.answer: Explain commercialisation as a sequence of linked capabilities, not as a simple shift from “traditional” to “modern.”.

stages.title: READING AGRICULTURE CURRENT AFFAIRS WITHOUT DATA MISTAKES
stages.terms: Use dated evidence as a labelled example: “PIB, 28 May 2025, records Kharif MSP approval; this is a policy announcement, not procurement coverage.”.
stages.mechanism: A national Kharif MSP announcement affects expectations across crop belts, but actual purchase still depends on crop, state, mandi access and procurement arrangements.
stages.consequence: Use dated evidence as a labelled example: “PIB, 28 May 2025, records Kharif MSP approval; this is a policy announcement, not procurement coverage.”.
stages.trap: It is not evidence of final output or universal procurement.
stages.answer: The Basic owner's current anchor is PIB, 28 May 2025, on approval of MSP for Kharif crops for 2025-26.

stages.title: NON-FARM PRIMARY ACTIVITIES — THE PHYSIOGRAPHY PRINCIPLE
stages.terms: Their location is tightly constrained because the resource cannot be shifted to any chosen place.
stages.mechanism: Their location is tightly constrained because the resource cannot be shifted to any chosen place.
stages.consequence: Do not list activities without the physiographic mechanism.
stages.trap: Resource occurrence is not the same as realised production.
stages.answer: Physiography sets where the resource can exist; human systems decide whether and how it is used.

stages.title: FISHING
stages.terms: Physiography explains potential, not landings by itself.
stages.mechanism: Fishing geography depends on the width and depth of the continental shelf, nutrient supply, current mixing, upwelling, sheltered landing sites, estuaries and inland water bodies.
stages.consequence: Mangrove-estuarine margins are nursery habitats but can also face aquaculture pressure.
stages.trap: The Gangetic and Brahmaputra floodplains and peninsular reservoirs also show why a major fish-producing area need not be coastal.
stages.answer: Coastal state does not automatically mean the same fishing potential.

stages.title: FORESTRY AND FOREST PRODUCE
stages.terms: Forestry is controlled not only by the existence of trees but by species, slope, distance and access.
stages.mechanism: Forestry is controlled not only by the existence of trees but by species, slope, distance and access.
stages.consequence: Do not treat all Indian forests as commercial timber zones.
stages.trap: Non-timber forest produce—bamboo, tendu leaf, mahua, gums, resins, honey, lac and medicinal plants—is especially important in central Indian and north-eastern forest belts.
stages.answer: Forestry location is shaped by forest type, slope, accessibility and rights.

stages.title: MINING AND QUARRYING
stages.terms: Quarrying may be widespread, but riverbed mining and hill cutting can destabilise channels and slopes.
stages.mechanism: The coincidence of mineral belts with peninsular plateaus shows the geological control.
stages.consequence: Mineral richness does not guarantee local prosperity.
stages.trap: Deposit quality alone does not decide viability.
stages.answer: Quarrying may be widespread, but riverbed mining and hill cutting can destabilise channels and slopes.
